update.title: Ported XFCE’s Whisker Menu to Wayfire
update.summary: Adapted XFCE’s searchable application launcher for a Wayland/Wayfire desktop, preserving its familiar menu workflow while adding compositor-aware focus handling.

blocks.body:
## Bring the XFCE application launcher into Wayfire

Whisker Menu provides the XFCE panel with searchable applications, categories, favorites, and a recent-launch list. I kept that familiar launcher while moving the desktop to Wayfire, adapting the maintained plugin rather than replacing its application model.

The port uses the plugin’s GTK layer-shell support for Wayland placement and preserves its normal search, selection, and launch behavior inside the XFCE panel.

blocks.label: XFCE migration: the panel and retained desktop forks

blocks.description: Whisker Menu showing favorite applications alongside categories such as accessories, graphics, internet, multimedia, office, settings, and system. blocks.body:
## Fill the Wayland focus gap

Layer-shell positioning did not provide the X11 focus signal Whisker Menu used to close after a click elsewhere. The port binds the wlroots foreign-toplevel-management protocol exposed by Wayfire, tracks activation for the menu’s toplevel, and schedules the existing GTK hide path when that activation is lost.

Generated protocol bindings and C++ lifecycle cleanup keep the integration contained. On X11, the Wayland monitor remains inactive and the original behavior continues.
